dedupe_keys.name: disaster risk assessment for the republic of croatia procjena rizika od katastrofa 2019

description: The disaster risk assessment for the Republic of Croatia is a 180-page PDF adopted by the Croatian Government under the Civil Protection System Act, published on the civil protection website. It was prepared by the main working group of the Croatian Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction, coordinated by the Ministry of the Interior, with representatives of the State Geodetic Administration, the Meteorological and Hydrological Service, the Bureau of Statistics, Croatian Waters, the ministries for construction, culture, sea and transport, defence, agriculture, environment and energy and health, and the Seismological Service. It sets out scenarios for plant and animal diseases, extreme temperatures, epidemics and pandemics, industrial accidents, river floods, earthquakes, open fires, snow and ice, drought, soil salinisation, nuclear and radiological accidents, landslides and marine pollution, plus a complex-risk scenario of floods caused by a strong earthquake in the City of Zagreb. It compares risks in matrices of worst-case and most likely events, reviews uncertainties, analyses civil protection preparedness, and takes the effect of climate change into account for each scenario. Access is free as a PDF; no licence is stated in the document. Caveats: the document is in Croatian, it is an assessment, not raw data, and the scenario elaborations are in an annex. Coverage is Croatia. It supports multi-hazard exposure and emergency response planning for infrastructure; related records are the National Disaster Risk Profile of Bulgaria and the Ireland National Risk Assessment 2023.
